Parse dates and times, in parallel

Source: R/par-as-date.R
par_as_date.Rd

Same results as base for strings, but much faster for large inputs:

  • par_as_date() for as.Date().

  • par_as_posixct() for as.POSIXct().

Base R takes seconds to parse a million dates, on one thread.

Usage

par_as_date(
  x,
  format,
  tryFormats = c("%Y-%m-%d", "%Y/%m/%d"),
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_as_posixct(
  x,
  tz = "",
  format,
  tryFormats = c("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS", "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%OS",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M", "%Y-%m-%d", "%Y/%m/%d"),
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

Arguments

x

A string vector, or a factor.

format

a character string. If not specified when converting from a character representation, it will try tryFormats one by one on the first non-NA element, and give an error if none works. Otherwise, the processing is via strptime() whose help page describes available conversion specifications.

tryFormats

character vector of format strings to try if format is not specified.

optional

logical indicating to return NA (instead of signalling an error) if the format guessing does not succeed.

...

Passed on to base R where it takes over.

nthreads

A whole number: the max number of threads to use. 0 means the RAYON_NUM_THREADS environment variable, or else all cores. The default is the parvenu.threads option, or 0 if that isn't set. Inputs too small to keep that many threads busy get fewer, and more threads than cores count as all cores.

tz

a time zone name.

Value

As as.Date(): a Date vector as long as x, NA where a string doesn't parse. par_as_posixct() returns a POSIXct vector instead, as as.POSIXct() does.

Details

Formats may use %Y, %y, %m, %b, %d, %e, %j, %H, %I with %p, %M, %S, %OS, %z (an offset such as +0530), %F, %T, and %R. %B and %h are read as %b: English month names, full or abbreviated to three letters, in any case. This works where the LC_TIME locale is C or English. A format needs a year, and a month and day or a day of the year, as the default tryFormats have.

Strings are read as strptime() reads them, quirks included. Text after the format is ignored, "24:00:00" is midnight of the next day, and "2020-1-5" is a date.

In UTC ("UTC", "GMT", or "" in a session whose time zone is UTC), the parse returns the times directly. In other time zones, base R's own C code places the local times, so a time that doesn't exist there, or occurs twice, comes out as in base. It places only the start and end of each day without a change of clock, whose times then follow from them, and every time of days with one. Where the times span more days than there are times, base R reads them all, as it is faster there.

Factors are turned into strings first. Everything else goes to base R:

  • other formats, or several formats in format

  • month names in other locales

  • inputs that aren't strings or factors, or fewer than 1e4 of them

  • tryFormats with %j or %z

  • spaces other than ASCII ones

  • seconds written in hexadecimal, with more than 15 digits, or as nan(...)

  • an input that no format fits, which base R reports.

Examples

par_as_date(c("2024-02-29", "2024-02-30", NA))
#> [1] "2024-02-29" NA           NA          
par_as_date("05.03.2024", format = "%d.%m.%Y")
#> [1] "2024-03-05"
par_as_posixct(c("2024-03-05 14:30:00.25", "2024-03-05 24:00:00"), tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "2024-03-05 14:30:00 UTC" "2024-03-06 00:00:00 UTC"
par_as_posixct("5 Mar 2024 2:30 PM", format = "%d %b %Y %I:%M %p", tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "2024-03-05 14:30:00 UTC"
par_as_posixct("2024-03-05T14:30:00+0530", format = "%FT%T%z", tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "2024-03-05 09:00:00 UTC"
par_as_posixct("2024-03-05 14:30:00", tz = "Europe/Berlin")
#> [1] "2024-03-05 14:30:00 CET"
